To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the language µKlaim provides a simple and elegant way to program distributed systems with mobile processes and tuple spaces; (ii) the language µKLAIM-SEC is a secure extension of µKlaim, in the sense that the type system guarantees that no process will perform any operation that violates the access control policy; (iii) the type system of µKLAIM-sec is sound with respect to the operational semantics of µKlaims.
we have designed and implemented a type system for µKlaim, which is sound, and which supports dynamic variations of the security policy.
we have designed and developed a type system for a process language that supports dynamic variations of security polices, and proved its soundness with respect to absence of run-time type errors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
providing a formal basis for a secure and efficient implementation of a distributed process language with mobile agents.
the design and implementation of a type system that can be used to enforce security policies on mobile code.
a language that is both expressive and secure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the type system we present is a sound and complete mechanism for controlling the activities of the processes in the net.
the type system is sound and complete, in a sense that can be made more precise.
we have developed a language for mobile code and a type system that guarantees that a mobile code system will be secure, i.e. that it will not violate any access and mobility policies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the programmer with a flexible and expressive tool to control access to resources and the mobility of processes in a distributed environment.
we provide a formal model for a process language that supports mobility and resource access control.
we have developed a type system for a mobile process calculus with a dynamic notion of privilege acquisition, and we have proved its soundness with respect to two different notions of correctness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the type system is able to deal with dynamic changes to the security policies of the net, and with the mobility of components.
it shows that a type system can be designed to control access to resources, mobility and dynamic privileges acquisition in a distributed environment.
the combination of dynamic privileges acquisition, static and dynamic type checks, and of inlining of reference monitors can be used to guarantee absence of errors in the presence of mobility.
